reason: The citation and mechanism are accurate: ArenaInstance.java:1123 is verbatim `if (getPlayerCount() < getMinPlayers()) {`, getPlayerCount() is `players.size()` (line 1069-1071, membership), while every liveness consumer (broadcastI18n:1021, onGameStart teleport loop:1264, stopGame kick loop:769, empty-arena task:1205) iterates getPlayers() which filters `player.isOnline()` (line 268). Under `auto-leave-on-quit: false`, MultiArenaManager.handleQuit (line 151) keeps the UUID and only opens a PendingRejoin, so quit does not shrink `players`; the only prune is expirePendingRejoins -> arena.removeOfflinePlayer (MultiArenaManager.java:113), which fires after `rejoin-timeout-seconds: 60` (game-settings.yml:37) versus `start-countdown: 10` (arenas.yml:182) — too late to cancel the countdown, so nothing refutes reachability. At countdown zero the task only does `cancelCountdown(); setState(GameState.RUNNING);` (lines 1139-1143); onGameStart has no online-count recheck and GameManager.startGame re-validates with the same membership set (`if (players.size() < getArenaMinPlayers()) return;`, GameManager.java:250), so a zero-online match genuinely starts and spawns villagers/waves. However the finding overstates severity: it is gated on the non-default, documented `auto-leave-on-quit: true`/ArenaManager.java:275 default, requires ALL members to disconnect inside a 10s window, and is self-healing — the empty-arena task is held off only while rejoins are pending (line 1212), rejoin expiry then drives removeOfflinePlayer -> `players.size() < getArenaMinPlayers() && isGameRunning()` -> endGame(false) (GameManager.java:740), and reset/completeResetAfterRestore reopen the arena, so the outage is ~25-90s rather than persistent, with no data destruction, crash, or economy exploit. The claimed 'false loss statistics' is partly by-design: retaining a member is the documented meaning of auto-leave-on-quit=false, so the retained member is treated as having lost the abandoned match.
counter_evidence:
auto-leave-on-quit: true  (src/main/resources/arenas.yml:176)

arena.removeOfflinePlayer(entry.getKey(), pending.playerName());  (MultiArenaManager.java:113 — prunes offline members, but only after rejoin-timeout-seconds: 60, i.e. after the 10s countdown has already started the match)
